clue.text: Easy, being a hero!

parts.note: Mr ... Easy is the title hero of Captain Marryat's naval novel, so the rank that goes with the name Easy is wanted

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that heroism comes easily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Easy' looks like an adjective but is the surname of the hero of Frederick Marryat's 1836 novel 'Mr Midshipman Easy'.
explanation.definitionFit: The hero of Marryat's novel holds the junior naval officer's rank named in its title.

clue.text: It takes me a jiffy to jot it down

definitions.text: It takes me a jiffy to jot it down

parts.note: taken as written
a mo is a moment, an instant, just like a jiffy

explanation.surface: Someone boasts that writing a quick note takes no time at all.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief written reminder is the kind of note one jots down in a moment.

clue.text: Record is found in the Washington district

indicators.note: being found in something means sitting inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: DC, the District of Columbia, is the federal district containing Washington
taken as written

explanation.surface: A record turns up in a part of the US capital.
explanation.definitionFit: A gramophone record is a flat disc of vinyl.

clue.text: Physicians give a capital address

parts.note: a London street famous for private doctors' consulting rooms, an address in the capital that physicians put on their letterheads

explanation.surface: Doctors deliver an excellent speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital address' reads as a fine speech, but means a street in London, the capital; HARLEY STREET is the London street known for private medical practices.
explanation.definitionFit: Harley Street in London is where many eminent doctors have their consulting rooms, so they give it as their address.

clue.text: Cinema in a Spanish market-place?

definitions.meaning: ... was a common name for picture houses, such as the ... in London's Lower Regent Street
in Spanish towns the open public square used for markets

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a picture house stands in a Spanish town square.
explanation.definitionFit: Plaza was a popular cinema name, and a Spanish town's open square serves as its market-place.

clue.text: Legal measures about possible visit of ginger group

indicators.note: one piece wrapped about another means the first goes around the second

parts.note: acts of Parliament are legal measures

indicators.note: a possible version of the word is one of its potential rearrangements

explanation.surface: New laws concern a prospective trip by a pressure group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ginger group' looks like red-haired people but is a British term for a faction pushing a larger body to act; 'about' wraps the shuffled visit letters ('possible') inside the measures.
explanation.definitionFit: A ginger group is a band of campaigners spurring others to action, which is what these militants are.

clue.text: Football team's singular incentive?

indicators.note: making the plural team name singular drops its final plural letter

parts.note: Spurs is the nickname of Tottenham Hotspur, the London football club

explanation.surface: Someone asks what motivates one particular football club.
explanation.walkthrough: Spurs is the nickname of Tottenham Hotspur, a London football club; 'singular' removes the plural S.
explanation.definitionFit: A spur is a goad or stimulus urging someone on.

clue.text: Load-up test can be taken for granted

indicators.note: the letters can be made into something else, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A loading test may be assumed to pass.
explanation.walkthrough: The ten letters of LOAD-UP TEST are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To postulate is to assume something as a basis for argument without proof.

clue.text: Compensating for Russian singers' embarrassment

annotationWithheld.why: Compensating for Russian singers' embarrassment: 'Compensating' defines REDRESSING but no sound parse of 'Russian singers' embarrassment' was found

clue.text: Oddly, misers can't be scoundrels

indicators.note: doing something oddly means doing it strangely, so the letters are set out in a strange order

explanation.surface: Strangely, skinflints are unable to be villains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' could suggest taking odd letters, but it is the anagram signal for MISERS CANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Miscreants are wrongdoers or villains.

clue.text: No new American press chief

parts.note: US is the abbreviation for American, as in the United States
ED is short for editor, the head of a newspaper

explanation.surface: No fresh news from the American head of the press.
explanation.definitionFit: Something second-hand is not new.

clue.text: He hunts for hidden mikes, under another name

definitions.text: He hunts for hidden mikes, under another name

parts.words: He hunts for hidden mikes, under another name
parts.note: hidden microphones are called bugs, so someone who hunts bugs under another name is an insect scientist

explanation.surface: A spy-catcher sweeps rooms for listening devices while using an alias.
explanation.walkthrough: Hidden mikes are 'bugs', and 'bugs' is another name for insects, the quarry of this scientist.
explanation.definitionFit: An insect specialist studies creatures popularly called bugs.

clue.text: Maybe the traveller goes .back before coming to the river

indicators.note: a word that goes back is read from end to start

parts.note: a rep is a commercial traveller, a sales representative
advent means arrival or coming
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: Perhaps the wanderer turns round before reaching the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes back' turns REP into PER. Peradventure is an archaic word for perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Peradventure is an old-fashioned word for perhaps or by chance.

clue.text: Untruthful about repair bill debts

parts.note: to mend is to repair
a/c is an account, a bill
IOUs are written promises to pay, so debts

explanation.surface: Someone lies about the cost of repairs and what is owed.
explanation.definitionFit: A mendacious person is given to lying.

clue.text: He's bound to learn something

parts.note: bound reads as certain, but here means tied by indentures to a master in order to learn a trade

explanation.surface: Someone is sure to pick up a thing or two.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bound' means certain on the surface, but an apprentice was legally bound by indentures to a master.
explanation.definitionFit: A trainee bound by contract to an employer learns a trade.

clue.text: Revelations made by scandal-mongers — or in camera?

definitions.meaning: disclosures of discreditable facts by gossips and tabloids
photographs taken on film inside a camera; in camera also suggests in private

explanation.surface: Scandal-sheets reveal secrets, or perhaps they are kept private.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in camera' means in private, a misleading contrast with the revelations; literally, film frames are exposed inside a camera.
explanation.definitionFit: Unmaskings of scandal are revelations, and frames of film shot in a camera bear the same name.

clue.text: Forgiveness of sin is more tricky

indicators.note: tricky suggests something twisted and awkward, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Pardoning a wrongdoing is harder than it looks.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of SIN IS MORE are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Remission of sins is their pardon or forgiveness.

clue.text: They're held by a jeweller's shop also

definitions.text: They're held by a jeweller's shop also

indicators.note: letters held by words are contained within them, across the gap

explanation.surface: Gems are stocked by a jeweller's shop too.
explanation.definitionFit: These iridescent gemstones are stock items at a jeweller's.

clue.text: German artist last seen in France

definitions.meaning: the great Nuremberg painter and engraver of the Renaissance, famous for woodcuts
in French the verb meaning to last, endure, is spelt this way

explanation.surface: A German painter was most recently spotted in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last seen' looks like the final sighting, but 'last' is a verb, and 'in France' asks for its French form.
explanation.definitionFit: Albrecht Dürer was a German Renaissance artist, and in French the verb for to endure is spelt the same.

clue.text: Anarchic ring moves to rule badly

indicators.note: anarchic means disordered, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A lawless gang acts to govern incompetently.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of RING MOVES are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To misgovern is to govern poorly.

clue.text: A chatty sort of piece?

parts.note: a painting showing a group in an informal setting is named after talk, which is a chatty thing; it is also an object that gets people talking

explanation.surface: Someone asks what a talkative item might be.
explanation.definitionFit: A conversation piece is a genre painting of an informal group, or an object prompting discussion, so talk is the chatty kind of piece.

clue.text: The marine engineer's.subject

parts.note: taken as written
ME is the abbreviation for marine engineer

explanation.surface: What a ship's engineer is interested in.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme is the topic of a talk or piece of writing.

clue.text: More than one such excursion to a French city

definitions.text: More than one such excursion to a French city

parts.words: More than one such excursion to a French city
parts.note: the plural of the word for an excursion is also the name of a city on the Loire

explanation.surface: Several trips are made to a city in France.
explanation.walkthrough: TOURS, the plural, is a city on the Loire, so one excursion is this singular word.
explanation.definitionFit: A tour is an excursion, and its plural names the French city of Tours.

clue.text: Strange point considered by our betters

parts.note: odd means strange
S is south, a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A peculiar matter is weighed up by our social superiors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'our betters' reads as social superiors but means people who bet, who study the prices offered.
explanation.definitionFit: Gamblers study the betting prices, so these are what punters consider.

clue.text: Poet of instinctive impulse, we hear?

indicators.note: what we hear is spoken, so the phrase is replaced by one that sounds the same

parts.note: the id is the instinctive impulses in Freudian theory, so of the id is of instinctive impulse

explanation.surface: Someone asks if this verse-writer was driven by instinct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of id' said quickly sounds like the name of the Roman poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovid was the Roman poet who wrote the Metamorphoses.

clue.text: Dagger found in a monastery room

definitions.meaning: a medieval thin-bladed knife used to deliver the death stroke, the stroke of mercy
a room in a monastery where some relaxation of the rule was permitted

explanation.surface: A dagger turns up in a monk's chamber.
explanation.definitionFit: A misericord was both a mercy-stroke dagger and a monastery room where relaxations were allowed.

clue.text: Cook fish found in this pond

definitions.meaning: to simmer slowly is to cook
a pond or tank where fish are kept for the table

explanation.surface: A chef prepares the fish taken from this pool.
explanation.walkthrough: As a noun this is an old word for a fishpond, where fish were kept until eaten.
explanation.definitionFit: To cook slowly in liquid is to stew, and a stew is also a pond for keeping fish.

clue.text: Deeds of the fashionable -dining sets

parts.note: in means fashionable
false teeth are sets used for eating, so dining sets

explanation.surface: The doings of the smart dinner-party crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dining sets' suggests tableware or social groups, but means sets of false teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: Indentures are legal contracts, formal deeds binding an apprentice.
